🇲🇽🛢️ <u>They Call Sovereignty a "Trade Barrier"</u>

As the T-MEC review heads into its next round, Washington is formally listing Sheinbaum's laws that restored Pemex and CFE as "barriers to investment." Behind that complaint sit BlackRock, Vanguard and Iberdrola — a decade after the 2013 neoliberal reform handed 41% of Mexico's power generation to ten private corporations. Mexico's answer caps private participation at 46% and puts the public grid first; the CFE that Washington wants clipped still generates nearly 40% of the country's electricity.

🇲🇽✈️ <u>Mexico's State Airline Keeps Climbing</u>

Mexicana de Aviación — the carrier the state brought back from the dead and now flies out of the army-built AIFA airport — took delivery of its ninth Embraer E190-E2, lifting capacity 11% to 57,020 seats a month. It's the 9th of 20 jets ordered directly from Embraer in 2024, with the full fleet due by 2027, as a public company rebuilds the national connectivity private carriers walked away from.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Even Washington's Own Ambassador Has to Admit It</u>

After Trump branded Mexico a narco-state and threatened intervention, his own ambassador Ronald Johnson conceded that Claudia Sheinbaum's government has dismantled more than 2,700 clandestine drug labs — the latest four in Michoacán and Guerrero, where security forces seized and destroyed over 10 metric tons of chemical precursors even after cartel gunmen opened fire on them. "Each laboratory destroyed means fewer deadly drugs reaching our communities," Johnson admitted.

🇲🇽🏭 Mexicana de Aviación keeps growing — the state airline just took delivery of its 9th jet. The publicly owned carrier received its ninth Embraer E190-E2 at AIFA, lifting capacity about 11% to 57,020 seats a month. It's part of a 20-plane order (10 E190-E2 + 10 E195-E2). The goal, in the airline's words: "connect Mexico with Mexico" and drive regional development — a public alternative rebuilt after decades of privatization. — Mexicana de Aviación · 20 Sep 2026

🇲🇽🌎 "Among individuals, as among nations, respect for the rights of others is peace." Quoting Benito Juárez, Sheinbaum tied today's defense of sovereignty to Mexico's long history of resisting foreign intervention — and contrasted it with the neoliberal era she called "36 years of darkness for Mexico." The lesson she drew for Sinaloa: peace comes with justice, freedom and sovereignty. — Claudia Sheinbaum, Culiacán, Sinaloa · 20 Sep 2026

🇲🇽🌎 "No foreign power decides the future of the homeland — nor does any elite. The future of the homeland is the people of Mexico." As Washington escalates talk of unilateral action against cartels on Mexican soil, Sheinbaum drew the line in Culiacán: no foreign government's interference in Mexican territory. Mexicans define their own future — and in Sinaloa, it is decided by the people of Sinaloa. — Claudia Sheinbaum, Culiacán, Sinaloa · 20 Sep 2026

🇲🇽✊ "It's love turned into politics — love turned into government action, love for the people." In Culiacán, Sheinbaum tallied what the wellbeing state has delivered in Sinaloa: the minimum wage rose from 2,800 pesos a month in 2018 to more than 9,500 today, and 1,128,000 sinaloenses — in a state of roughly 3 million people — receive a wellbeing program directly. — Claudia Sheinbaum, Culiacán, Sinaloa · 20 Sep 2026

🇲🇽🌎 "No foreign power, no elite, defines the future of the nation. That is the independence of Mexico." Tracing Mexico's history from Hidalgo and Morelos to today, Sheinbaum answered those who call for foreign intervention in the month of independence: "We say: never. Mexico is a free, independent and sovereign country — it cost us dearly to reach this moment." — Claudia Sheinbaum — La Paz, Baja California Sur
